summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea lasting one month, in the context of multiple comorbidities including common variable immunodeficiency, large cell lymphoma in remission, and colostomy status. She also reported orthostatic dizziness and new left shoulder pain. Workup included a CT abdomen and pelvis showing stable retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and no acute abdominal findings, a normal shoulder X-ray, and a colonoscopy with unremarkable findings and pending biopsies. Stool studies were negative for C. diff, parasites, and CMV. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics initiated in clinic and continued on ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, along with loperamide and dicyclomine for symptom control. Her symptoms improved during the hospitalization, dizziness resolved, and she was discharged home on a full course of oral antibiotics and updated symptom management medications. Follow-up was arranged for shoulder pain if persistent, strongyloides IgG results, and colonoscopy biopsies.
